passage: Have you ever wondered how we coat a metal spoon with silver or why some liquids conduct electricity while others do not? Electricity flowing through a liquid causes chemical changes, a process called electrolysis. When we perform electroplating, the metal from the electrolyte solution is deposited onto the object. It is not the electricity itself that turns into metal; instead, the metal ions already present in the solution move and settle on the object. Pure distilled water is actually a poor conductor because it lacks dissolved salts. However, when we add substances like salt or lemon juice, the liquid becomes a good conductor. You might notice bubbles forming near the electrodes during this process. These bubbles are not steam from boiling water, but are actually gases released due to the chemical reaction. Furthermore, a simple bulb tester might not glow even if a tiny current is flowing, because some liquids conduct electricity very weakly. In such cases, we use a magnetic compass to detect the current. Finally, remember that electroplating is used to protect metals from corrosion, not to make them stronger. The metal atoms travel through the liquid electrolyte as ions, not through the air, to reach the electrode.

items.evidence: It is not the electricity itself that turns into metal; instead, the metal ions already present in the solution move and settle on the object.
items.q: When a spoon is silver plated, where does the silver coating come from?
options: From silver ions already in the solution
From the electricity changing into silver
From silver atoms flying across through air
From the spoon's own metal turning silver
items.explain: Electricity does not become metal; silver ions already in the solution move and settle on the spoon.

wrong.why: thinks metal travels through the air
thinks the object itself changes colour

items.evidence: However, when we add substances like salt or lemon juice, the liquid becomes a good conductor.
items.q: Distilled water barely conducts electricity. What would make it a good conductor?
options: Dissolving some common salt in it
Pouring in more pure distilled water
Heating it until it starts to boil
Putting a magnetic compass into it
items.explain: Distilled water lacks dissolved salts; adding salt or lemon juice makes it a good conductor.

wrong.why: thinks distilled water already conducts well
thinks a magnet changes the liquid

items.evidence: These bubbles are not steam from boiling water, but are actually gases released due to the chemical reaction.
items.q: Bubbles form near the electrodes, yet the water stays cool. What are these bubbles?
options: Gases given off by a chemical change
Steam from water that is starting to boil
Air that was trapped inside the wires
Tiny bits of metal leaving the plates
items.explain: The bubbles are gases released by the chemical reaction, not steam from boiling water.

wrong.why: thinks bubbles mean the water is boiling
guesses the bubbles come from the wires
thinks metal jumps off the plates

items.evidence: Furthermore, a simple bulb tester might not glow even if a tiny current is flowing, because some liquids conduct electricity very weakly.
items.q: Ali's tester bulb stays dark in a liquid, but a compass needle moves. What does this show?
options: The liquid carries a very weak current
The liquid carries no current at all
The liquid has become a magnet itself
The liquid only holds up the wires
items.explain: Some liquids conduct very weakly, so the bulb stays dark while a tiny current still flows.

wrong.why: thinks a dark bulb means no current
thinks the liquid turns into a magnet
thinks the liquid plays no part

items.evidence: Finally, remember that electroplating is used to protect metals from corrosion, not to make them stronger.
items.q: Why might a factory electroplate its iron parts?
options: To protect them from rusting away
To make them harder and stronger
To fill them with metal made by electricity
To make them carry electricity better
items.explain: Electroplating protects metals from corrosion; it does not make them stronger.

wrong.why: mixes up plating with conducting electricity
